## Context / Problem
Split out of bug adb6-4762-90f6-4e30 (peach-chemic-hairstreak) by operator ruling (2026-08-21): the fresh-shell fix pins bedrock_region_name = "us-east-1" in rebar.toml's [llm] table, but the verdict's provider provenance cannot yet truthfully record that the region came from repo config.

RCA finding (proven statically on the bug ticket, 2026-08-17): LLMConfig.from_env collapses CLI/env/config-file resolution of bedrock_region_name into ONE string via _llm_str (src/rebar/llm/config.py), discarding the value's origin. resolve_bedrock_region (src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py) then labels EVERY configured non-empty value as region_source=REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION — so a rebar.toml pin is mislabeled as the env var in provenance records (pinned today by tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py, which asserts region_source == "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" for a configured region).

## Approach
Add source metadata/plumbing so provenance records region_source truthfully ("repo-config" for the config-file table, "cli" for `rebar -c llm.bedrock_region_name=…`, and the existing "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" / "AWS_DEFAULT_REGION" / "AWS_REGION" labels), without changing which value wins. The label is derived from the SAME single resolution pass that produced the value (a source-returning variant of _llm_str that _llm_str delegates to), carried on LLMConfig as bedrock_region_source, and threaded to resolve_bedrock_region / provenance_for — never re-derived independently, so record and runtime cannot diverge. Operator caution (recorded on the bug ticket): provenance labeling may interact with config wiring and env-var handling — design to avoid regression there, and maintain portability across diverse environments (no CI-provider-specific trigger; see project.portability).

## File impact
- src/rebar/llm/config.py — carry the resolved region's origin (do not regress _llm_str precedence: CLI > env > file > default)
- src/rebar/llm/bedrock_model.py — resolve_bedrock_region labels the configured value by its true source
- src/rebar/llm/capabilities.py — provenance_for threads the configured source into the resolver
- src/rebar/llm/runner.py — thread cfg.bedrock_region_source alongside cfg.bedrock_region_name
- tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py, tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py — update/extend the pins

## Testing
RED first: extend `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` and `tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` with the truthful-label pins (they fail against the current always-REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION labeling), then implement. Prove with:
- `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py` — the full precedence+label matrix and the provenance record pins.
- `pytest tests/unit/test_llm_config.py tests/unit/test_llm_model_env_removal.py` (or the nearest config-layer suites) — no regression in the CLI > env > file resolution wiring.
- `make lint` and `make typecheck` — the complexity ratchet and types stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] A region resolved from the config-file table is recorded in provider provenance as region_source="repo-config", not "REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION" (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py`).
- [ ] A region resolved from the REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION env var keeps region_source="REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION"; AWS_DEFAULT_REGION / AWS_REGION keep their existing labels (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_verdict_provenance.py tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [ ] A region resolved from `rebar -c llm.bedrock_region_name=…` is labeled "cli" (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [ ] Resolution precedence is unchanged: CLI > REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_REGION > config file, then AWS_DEFAULT_REGION > AWS_REGION; every source combination's precedence+label pair is pinned (verified: `pytest tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py`).
- [ ] The resolved region VALUE and every provider build path are byte-identical for identical inputs — the label is additive metadata only (verified: the existing build-path tests in `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py` pass with no wiring changes).
- [ ] Works with no CI provider present: pure in-process labeling with nothing CI-specific (checked: the diff touches only library code + unit tests, no CI-provider hooks).
